exposure: uterine rupture of a scarred uterus
cohort: Women with uterine rupture (126 with scarred uterus, 20 with unscarred uterus)
finding: Primary uterine rupture is associated with higher maternal morbidity, including blood loss, transfusion rates, and hysterectomy, as well as increased risk of adverse neonatal neurologic outcomes.
mod_finding: Women with primary uterine rupture delivering vaginally were more likely to ultimately undergo hysterectomy than those delivering by cesarean (63% vs 9%; P = .017).
